stage_2.note: Three factual corrections (IHC hospital count → two primary-filing sources = High; specialist deficit → two primary-gov sources = High; Peka B40 → two secondary sources citing institutional primary = Medium). unique_urls_total.method: Count of unique domains + page paths across all stage source lists. Includes Stage 1 (55 URLs noted in deep-research addendum) + Stage 2 (~30 unique additional) + Stage 3 (~35 unique additional, some overlap with S1–S2 for CodeBlue, PMC, OJK) + Stages 4–6 fresh sources (F1–F18 in Stage 5, ~15 additional in Stage 6). Estimated overlap-adjusted unique URL count: ~98.
unique_urls_total.note: Target was 40–60 unique URLs. Actual corpus exceeds the upper bound at ~98 URLs. This is not a quality problem — the excess reflects comprehensive coverage across three market layers and two countries. However, it underscores that de-duplication is needed: many URLs are cited across multiple stages (see sources_used_multiple_stages below).

cross_stage_inconsistencies.detail: Stage 1, 2, and 4 initially cite '8.9% of eligible FKTPs have activated an EMR' as the SATUSEHAT adoption rate. Deep-research Upgrade 3 clarifies this is PT MTK's vendor market share, not the national SATUSEHAT integration rate. Stages 1–2 draft text uses this figure to justify 'near-zero' private clinic EMR adoption. Post-deep-research, the correct framing is 'MOH Digital Health Blueprint 2024 acknowledges 80% of facilities lack digital technology' — directionally consistent but the specific 8.9% should not appear as the SATUSEHAT integration rate in any stage. Stages 4 and 5 are updated to use the MOH Blueprint framing. Stage 2 (PP2.1-k) still references the 8.9% from the preprint — correction required in canonical artifact.
cross_stage_inconsistencies.severity: medium — direction of claim (low private clinic EMR adoption) is confirmed; the specific 8.9% figure is incorrectly attributed
cross_stage_inconsistencies.resolution: Apply Stage 1 deep-research addendum Upgrade 3 framing across all stages: replace '8.9% of eligible FKTPs have activated SATUSEHAT' with '80% of facilities lack digital technology (MOH Digital Health Blueprint 2024); private klinik pratama are largely paper-based; hospital integration dominates SATUSEHAT headline count of 33,901–34,463 facilities'

cross_stage_inconsistencies.detail: Stage 3 initially states '2023 claims ratio reached ~111% for many product lines'. Stage 3 corrections addendum clarifies this is a multi-year BNM band (2018–2023 ex-pandemic) and the 2023 single-year LIAM ICR is 65.9%. cross_stage_inconsistencies.description: CDM leakage cascade mixes public and private sector proxies without consistent labelling
cross_stage_inconsistencies.detail: Stage 4 Section 4.4 constructs a 1,000 → 17 cascade using: Posbindu (public community screening) for Layer 1; South Korean semiconductor company onsite clinic (PMC 12021225) for Layer 2; Prolanis/BPJS East Java (PMC 12538241) for Layer 3; and NDR Malaysia for control. All four inputs are individually Low-confidence with setting/geography mismatches. Stage 5 presents the cascade as a central pillar of the Malaysia Layer 2 pilot recommendation. The uncertainty in the cascade is noted in Stage 4 ('illustrative cascade using best available evidence') but is not consistently flagged as Low-confidence in Stage 5's strategic recommendation.
cross_stage_inconsistencies.severity: medium — the cascade direction is defensible; quantified output (98.3% leakage) may be misleadingly precise given all four Low-confidence inputs
cross_stage_inconsistencies.resolution: Add explicit confidence tag to the WH5 cascade in Stage 5: 'CDM leakage cascade is an illustrative Low-confidence estimate using proxy data from four settings none of which match private GP clinic in ID/MY directly. Field validation of each leakage rate is the highest-priority empirical task.'

However Stage 5 similarly does not reference the corrected figure. The correction should be propagated to any canonical artifact that mentions IHC facility count.
cross_stage_inconsistencies.severity: low — Stage 4–5 do not cite IHC facility count directly; correction is confined to Stage 2 canonical artifact
cross_stage_inconsistencies.resolution: Apply Stage 2 corrections addendum Correction 1 to canonical Stage 2 artifact. No further propagation needed.

gate_reasoning: The corpus of 240 scored claims across 6 stages yields 18% High, 33% Medium, 49% Low post-deep-research corrections. This is below the typical 'ship-as-is' threshold (target: >30% High, <40% Low) but above the 're-run' threshold. The corpus has three distinct quality tiers: (1) Stages 4–6 synthesis stages are analytically rigorous and internally consistent despite deriving from Low-confidence inputs — their value is in the analytical framework, not individual data points, and should be clearly labelled as such; (2) Stage 3 (insurance/TPA) is the strongest empirical stage with 24% High and multiple confirmed primary-filing sources (Prodia, KPJ, Sinar Mas, Allianz, AAJI, LIAM, BNM); (3) Stage 1 (GP clinics) improved significantly post-deep-research from 80% Low to an estimated 64% Low, but structural Low-confidence issues remain in salary data, single-study US/global benchmarks, and the inaccessible NDR 2023. Five cross-stage inconsistencies were identified; all have documented corrections. Eight geography-mismatch flags span multiple stages, the most critical being the Korean semiconductor sector proxy for corporate MCU CDM follow-up rates (GM-2) and the InterPixels AI vendor benchmark for claims costs (GM-5). The corpus should ship with: (a) explicit confidence-tier labels on each sub-step in the canonical artifact; (b) ASSUMED-N tags visible in all cost estimates; (c) the Stage 1 SATUSEHAT adoption figure corrected corpus-wide; (d) the POJK designation corrected corpus-wide; and (e) the Malaysia NDR 2023 URL resolution as the single highest-impact pending action. The underlying research quality — two countries, three market layers, 12 sub-steps mapped, five working hypotheses tested — is strong and warrants shipping for editorial review with these flags applied.
notes: Total unique URL count (~98) exceeds the 40–60 target range. This reflects comprehensive multi-layer multi-country scope. De-duplication during canonical artifact build should identify ~20 URLs cited across 3+ stages for special corroboration annotation.

CodeBlue.galencentre.org is the single most-cited domain across all stages (appearing in Stages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Under single-domain override, no claim sourced exclusively from CodeBlue can exceed Medium confidence. CodeBlue is a legitimate and credible health trade publication in Malaysia; the single-domain constraint is a rubric artifact, not a quality judgment on CodeBlue.

InterPixels AI is the single most consequential auto-low-vendor source. Stages 3, 4, and 6 all rely on InterPixels benchmarks for claims cost and STP rate estimates. Every figure from interpixels.ai is auto-Low regardless of citation count. A KPMG, Deloitte, or McKinsey SEA insurance automation authored report would be the upgrade path.

The West Malaysian (Klang Valley / Penang) focus in Stages 1–3 means East Malaysia and non-Tier-1 Indonesian cities are not evidenced. All claims about clinic operations, MCU programmes, and TPA processing should carry an implicit 'Tier-1/2 city' qualifier.

Stage 6 ASSUMED-1 through ASSUMED-4 tags on language performance claims are the most material unknowns for commercial deployment feasibility. A controlled benchmark of LLM/ASR/NER on 200 real ID/MY clinical notes would resolve all four assumptions and would be the highest-impact technical validation ahead of any pilot.
